root_cause.text: The error path after a failed `aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices()` call in `nouveau_drm_probe` directly returns without freeing the `nvkm_device` allocated by `nvkm_device_pci_new()`, causing a resource leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the failing branch from `return ret;` to `goto fail_nvkm;`, ensuring `nvkm_device_del()` is called to unwind the allocation. The commit message states: "the error path returns directly without unwinding the nvkm_device that was just allocated by nvkm_device_pci_new(). This leaks both the device wrapper and the pci_enable_device() reference taken inside it." The fix was introduced by commit c0bfe34330b5 which moved device creation earlier but omitted the matching cleanup.

commit 2dd4d163cd9c15432524aa9863155bc03a821361
Author: Ben Skeggs <bskeggs@redhat.com>
Date:   Sun Feb 2 13:55:23 2020 +1000

    drm/nouveau: remove open-coded version of remove_conflicting_pci_framebuffers()
    
    Signed-off-by: Ben Skeggs <bskeggs@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_drm.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_drm.c
index ca4087f5a15b..eb10c80ed853 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_drm.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_drm.c
@@ -681,8 +68
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows that the call to `remove_conflicting_pci_framebuffers()` (which replaces the open-coded aperture removal) is placed before `nvkm_device_pci_new()`. If that call fails, the function returns immediately via `return ret;` without having allocated the nvkm_device. Consequently, there is no nvkm_device to free, and the leak described in the root cause (failure to free an already allocated nvkm_device) cannot occur. The code already has the correct ordering to prevent the vulnerability.
